Manufacturing/Assembly sequence

Manufacturing

How a power transformer is built.

Scroll to assemble a three-phase oil-immersed power transformer, from the bare core to a tested unit. Scroll back up to take it apart.

  1. 01 / 08

    Core

    Grain-oriented silicon-steel laminations are cut to length and stacked with step-lap joints to keep no-load loss and noise low. The top yoke is then unlaced so the windings can be lowered onto the limbs.

    Material
    Grain-oriented silicon steel
    Joints
    Step-lap, mitred
    Equipment
    Soenen cut-to-length line
  2. 02 / 08

    Windings

    Each limb takes a low-voltage winding next to the core and a high-voltage winding outside it, separated by pressboard cylinders and spacers. The top yoke is re-laced and the active part is clamped.

    Arrangement
    Concentric: LV inner, HV outer
    HV coils
    20 t horizontal winding machine
    LV coils
    Foil winding machine
  3. 03 / 08

    Leads and tap changer

    Winding ends are connected to the bushing leads, and tapping leads run to the tap changer: on-load (OLTC) for regulation in service, or off-circuit (OCTC) for settings chosen at commissioning.

    HV leads
    To HV bushings
    LV leads
    Copper bar, incl. neutral
    Tap changer
    OLTC or OCTC
    OLTC or OCTC?
  4. 04 / 08

    Vacuum drying

    The active part is heated under vacuum to draw moisture out of the cellulose insulation. It is re-clamped afterwards, because the insulation shrinks as it dries.

    Removes
    Moisture from paper and pressboard
    Then
    Re-clamping of the windings
  5. 05 / 08

    Tank, cover and bushings

    The dried active part goes into the welded tank without delay, the cover is bolted on and the high- and low-voltage bushings are mounted on it.

    Tank
    Robot-welded steel
    HV bushings
    3 phases
    LV bushings
    3 phases + neutral
  6. 06 / 08

    Oil filling

    Filtered, degassed insulating liquid is filled under vacuum so that no air stays trapped in the insulation, followed by a standing time before testing.

    Liquid
    Mineral oil or natural ester
    Method
    Filling under vacuum
    Mineral oil or natural ester?
  7. 07 / 08

    Cooling and conservator

    Radiators carry heat away by natural oil and air circulation (ONAN); fans add forced air (ONAF). The conservator takes up oil expansion, with a Buchholz relay and breather on its pipework.

    Cooling
    ONAN, ONAF with fans
    Protection
    Buchholz relay
    Breathing
    Silica-gel breather
    ONAN or ONAF?
  8. 08 / 08

    Tests and release

    Routine tests confirm every unit before shipment: ratio and vector group, winding resistance, no-load and load loss, impedance, applied and induced voltage, and partial discharge. Lightning impulse and temperature rise are added when specified.

    Lightning impulse
    2,400 kV test system
    Power frequency
    300 kV test system
    Partial discharge
    8-channel detector
    Test equipment

Where each step happens at Tianyu.

The same sequence runs through the Fuzhou manufacturing base, from core cutting and winding lines to the test laboratory.
